title: Universal injectivity, diagonal surjectivity and fullness on geometric groupoids
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, representability by algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; smoothness is tested on scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Its underlying point space consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$. Say that $f$ is universally injective if for every morphism of algebraic stacks $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$, the map $|\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z|\to|\mathcal Z|$ is injective. The following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is universally injective; (2) its relative diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is surjective on underlying points; (3) for every algebraically closed field $K$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] with $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, objects $x_1,x_2\in\mathcal X(K)$, and isomorphism $\beta:f(x_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}f(x_2)$ in $\mathcal Y(K)$, there is an isomorphism $\alpha:x_1\xrightarrow{\sim}x_2$ with $f(\alpha)=\beta$.

source.place: Tag 0CPN (lemma-universally-injective), including its complete statement; universal injectivity is definition-universally-injective in the same section.

proof.text: Set $P=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$; this is algebraic by the fibre-product lemma. Its objects are $(x_1,x_2,\beta)$, and an arrow to $(x'_1,x'_2,\beta')$ is a pair $(u,v)$ satisfying $f(v)\beta=\beta'f(u)$. The diagonal sends $x$ to $(x,x,\mathrm{id})$. Both projections composed with the diagonal are identities, and the two images of each point of $P$ in $|\mathcal Y|$ agree, because $\beta$ is an isomorphism. These assertions follow directly from the triple and arrow formulas.

source.place: Tag 0CPN, preliminary notation and triple construction

proof.text: Assume (1). The first projection $p_1:P\to\mathcal X$ is a base change of $f$, so $|p_1|$ is injective. For $t\in|P|$, put $a=|p_1|(t)$. Both $t$ and $|\Delta_f|(a)$ map to $a$ under $|p_1|$. Injectivity gives $t=|\Delta_f|(a)$, proving (2). This also covers an empty point set.

Assume (2), and take any $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y$. Put $W=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z$ and $h:W\to\mathcal Z$. The diagonal $\Delta_f$ is representable by the relative-diagonal lemma. Therefore its point-surjectivity is equivalent to surjectivity on every scheme base change. The chartwise calculus preserves this property under arbitrary base change. The map $W\times_{\mathcal Z}W\to P$ forgets the $\mathcal Z$-object and composes the comparison isomorphisms with the isomorphism between the two $\mathcal Z$-objects. Its pullback of $\Delta_f$ is $\Delta_h$: the data are two $W$-objects and a compatible isomorphism of their $\mathcal X$-components; together with the given isomorphism of their $\mathcal Z$-components this is exactly an arrow in $W$. Thus $|\Delta_h|$ is surjective, by the same representable-surjectivity criterion.

source.place: Tag 0CPN, (2) implies (1), first two sentences; explicit diagonal base-change identification

proof.text: If $a,b\in|W|$ have the same image in $|\mathcal Z|$, choose field representatives. Equality in $|\mathcal Z|$ means that over a common extension their images become isomorphic. The two representatives and that isomorphism give an object of $W\times_{\mathcal Z}W$ projecting to $a,b$. Surjectivity of $|\Delta_h|$ expresses its point as a diagonal point; its two projections are consequently equal. Hence $a=b$. Since $\mathcal Z$ was arbitrary, (1) follows. This is the point-cartesian argument written from the definition, without assuming that point sets preserve fibre products bijectively.

source.place: Tag 0CPN, (2) implies (1), last sentences; stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian), explicit common-field argument

proof.text: Assume (3), and represent any $t\in|P|$ over a field $L$. Extend $L$ to an algebraic closure $K$; pullback preserves its point class. Write its triple as $(x_1,x_2,\beta)$ over $K$. By (3) choose $\alpha:x_1\simeq x_2$ with $f(\alpha)=\beta$. The pair $(\mathrm{id}_{x_1},\alpha)$ is an arrow from $\Delta_f(x_1)$ to this triple, since its arrow equation is $f(\alpha)\mathrm{id}=\beta f(\mathrm{id})$. Thus $t$ is in the diagonal image, proving (2).

Assume (2), and fix the $K,x_1,x_2,\beta$ in (3). For $t=(x_1,x_2,\beta)$, the relative-diagonal lemma makes $T=\mathcal X\times_{P,t}\operatorname{Spec}K$ an algebraic space locally of finite type over $K$. The representable point-surjectivity criterion makes $T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ surjective, so $T$ is nonempty. Choose an etale surjective scheme chart $U\to T$. The chartwise calculus makes $U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ locally of finite type: etale implies smooth, hence locally finitely presented, hence locally of finite type, and such maps compose. Choose a nonempty affine finite-type open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $U$. The ring $A$ is nonzero; the maximal-ideal leaf supplies a maximal ideal. It gives a closed point $v$ of $V$. The closed-point residue-field lemma gives $\kappa(v)=K$ as $K$-fields, and the field-point classification gives a $K$-point of $V$, hence of $T$. Only $V$ is required to be affine or finite type; no quasi-compactness or separation of $T$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0CPN, (2) implies (3), through existence of a K-point of T; rational-point argument expanded on an affine etale chart

proof.text: A $K$-point of $T$ consists of $x\in\mathcal X(K)$ and an isomorphism from $\Delta_f(x)$ to $(x_1,x_2,\beta)$. Write its components $u:x\simeq x_1$, $v:x\simeq x_2$. The arrow equation is $f(v)=\beta f(u)$. Set $\alpha=v u^{-1}$. Then $f(\alpha)=f(v)f(u)^{-1}=\beta$, proving (3). The four implications prove the asserted equivalence; fullness asserts existence of a lift and does not assert uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 0CPN, (2) implies (3), final sentence, explicitly unwound
